messages:
mei: Heads-up: ran the new quantized xglm-7b (q4f16) bring-up eval on multilingual-latest. Noticed a big BLEU drop on zh-Hant and KO->JA. Also some detok mismatches around fullwidth punctuation + soft line breaks. Posting short summary.
eval-bot: Eval summary: model=xglm-7b-q4f16 | dataset=multilang-2026-v2 | pairs=[zh-Hant->en, ko->ja] | BLEU: zh-Hant->en: 29.4 (-6.7), ko->ja: 22.1 (-4.5) | chrF: -3.2 | COMET: -0.18. Top failure class: token-boundary merges near fullwidth '。' and unicode ellipsis '…' + linebreak join.
sam: :eyes: can you paste a minimal repro of the detok failure?
mei: Here's a short excerpt (source zh-Hant):
'第一行。
第二行…
第三行～結束'
Quantized output detok: '第一行第二行…第三行～結束' (linebreak removed). Host (non-quant) model output preserves linebreaks. Looks like something in token join/detok path changed.
jyoti: Hypothesis: merging happens when fullwidth punctuation becomes attached to preceding subword after quantization-induced merges. Could also be interaction with prefix/KV-cache slicing — if cache flush + reassembly path uses different detok rules we can lose explicit linebreak tokens. Also check tokenizer normalization flags (NFKC vs NFKD).
sam: I'll run a bisect across quant levels (int8, q4f16, q5_0, q8) and compare to cpu baseline. Running on staging now. Script: 
```
./eval/bisect_quant.sh --model xglm-7b --pairs zh-Hant-en ko-ja --seed 42
```
ETA ~30m.
ci-bot: Deploy note: job started on dedicated-staging/gpu-pool-b. Job id j-7893. Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/j-7893. Auto-retry enabled.
mei: Also seeing KO->JA examples where ASCII '...' or U+2026 '…' collapses into a single token and then merges with preceding Kana, causing suffix attachment and morphological changes. chrF / morph deltas point to suffix-level errors.
jyoti: Quick interim workaround: add a normalization preprocessor that substitutes explicit <NL> for line breaks and prevents joining on fullwidth punctuation, then detok with strict spacing rules. Can expose as feature flag tokenizer_config.preserve_linebreaks=true. Not ideal but low-effort to mitigate customer-facing regressions.
sam: :thumbsup: If the bisect shows quantizer is not the cause, I'll inspect runtime kernel selection and attention stride tie-breaks — those have flipped ordering in recent runtime patches and could influence token boundary generation order.
mei: Thanks all — I'll open an internal bug with minimal repro + failing examples once bisect finishes. Ping here if you see similar failures in other locales. :wave:
